title: Induced random mixed states are symmetric Dirichlet mixtures
authors: Brian T. Kirby, Alexander C. B. Greenwood, Sanjaya Lohani, Joseph M. Lukens
abstract: We establish an exact equivalence in distribution between $D$-dimensional random mixed states induced by partial traces over $K$-dimensional environments and the Mai-Alquier distribution, a mixture of $K$ independent Haar-random pure states weighted by a symmetric Dirichlet distribution. This identification recasts a class of expectation values for induced ensembles into calculations involving Dirichlet moments and low-order Haar averages on a single-system state space. As applications, we recover exact purity moments up to fourth order, derive the mean Hilbert--Schmidt distance between independent induced ensembles with possibly different environment dimensions, and obtain exact average determinants. These results provide a unified and constructive perspective on induced random mixed states and on the evaluation of quantities such as purity moments, overlaps, and determinants.
summary: This paper proves a deep mathematical equivalence between random mixed quantum states generated by tracing out an environment and a statistical mixture called the Mai-Alquier distribution. This identification is highly valuable because it allows researchers to calculate complex quantum observables, such as purity moments and determinants, using simpler tools from the theory of Dirichlet distributions and Haar averages. It unifies the theoretical understanding of induced random mixed states.
main_problem: The paper establishes an exact equivalence between random mixed states induced by tracing out an environment and a specific statistical mixture known as the Mai-Alquier (MA) distribution.
main_result: This equivalence allows complex calculations involving induced random mixed states (like purity moments and determinants) to be recast into manageable calculations involving Dirichlet moments and low-order Haar averages.
method: The authors use properties of the Ginibre ensemble and the Gamma distribution to show that the induced state distribution matches the Dirichlet-weighted mixture distribution when the Dirichlet parameter equals the system dimension.
model_or_system: The model involves a D-dimensional system coupled to a K-dimensional environment, prepared in a Haar-random pure global state, followed by tracing out the environment to yield the induced mixed state.
key_observables: Purity moments ($	ext{Tr} ho^m$), mean Hilbert-Schmidt distance between ensembles, and the determinant ($\det ho$).
important_parameters: D (system dimension), K (environment dimension), and the Dirichlet concentration parameter $\alpha$ (which must equal D for equivalence).
main_assumptions: The equivalence holds under the condition that the Dirichlet concentration parameter $\alpha$ matches the system dimension $D$.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the geometric equivalence for a qubit system, showing both the MA construction (convex combination) and the induced state construction using Ginibre matrix columns leading to the same Dirichlet law.
paper_structure: The paper first defines the induced state via partial traces over a random environment, then derives the statistical properties showing the equivalence to the MA distribution. It then applies this equivalence to derive exact formulas for key observables like purity moments, distance, and determinants.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful mathematical tool to simplify calculations in open quantum systems by mapping physical environmental tracing processes onto well-understood statistical ensembles (Dirichlet mixtures).

Left: A mixed state is formed by convexly combining K independent Haar-random pure states |ψj⟩with weights p ∼DirK(D). Right: The columns |˜gj⟩of a 2 × 3 Ginibre matrix (plotted as orange circles) determine normalized directions |ψj⟩= |˜gj⟩/∥|˜gj⟩∥(plotted as blue circles) and radial weights through trace normalization of GG†.
